request: Our FinOps analyst says our production Kubernetes cluster is 72% utilized and proposes replacing the 40 n4.large nodes with 20 n4.xlarge nodes, claiming this halves compute cost and saves about $2,800 a month because 'bigger nodes are more efficient'. The SRE team says the cluster is mostly idle. I need to decide whether to approve the node migration this month. The FinOps report, Nimbus Cloud price sheet and the SRE utilization dashboard export are attached.

fixtures.name: finops-report.md
fixtures.content:
# FinOps recommendation - prod-k8s (2026-10)

- Cluster utilization: 72% (CPU)
- Current: 40 x n4.large
- Proposed: 20 x n4.xlarge
- Estimated saving: 50% of node spend, ~$2,803/month
- Rationale: larger nodes reduce per-node overhead (kubelet, daemonsets).

fixtures.name: nimbus-price-sheet.csv
fixtures.content:

n4.large,4,16,0.192
n4.xlarge,8,32,0.384
n4.2xlarge,16,64,0.768
# Billing: 730 hours per month for estimates

fixtures.name: sre-dashboard-export.csv
fixtures.content:

cpu_used_pct_of_allocatable,31,30d avg
cpu_used_pct_of_allocatable_p95,44,30d
mem_requested_pct_of_allocatable,68,30d avg
mem_used_pct_of_allocatable,39,30d avg
daemonset_cpu_per_node_vcpu,0.25,

expected.summary: The claimed saving is wrong: 40 x $0.192 = $7.68/hour and 20 x $0.384 = $7.68/hour, so node spend is identical (about $5,606/month either way) and the swap saves roughly nothing beyond a small daemonset overhead reduction (about 0.25 vCPU per removed node). The two sources conflict because they measure different things: 72% is CPU requested, while actual usage is 31% average and 44% p95, so workloads are over-requesting. The real lever is rightsizing pod requests (and then letting the autoscaler remove nodes), plus considering committed-use or spot pricing. Do not approve the migration on the basis of the claimed $2,803 saving.

mustFlag.description: Cost is identical ($7.68/h both ways), no 50% saving
72% is requested, not used; actual usage ~31%

criticalFailures: Accepts that consolidating to 20 n4.xlarge halves cost or saves ~$2,800/month
Treats 72% requested CPU as actual utilization
